analyst_view.overall: Leeds come into this in good form: they beat Tottenham 1-0 before the international break and then won 4-1 at Chelsea on 21 November, with Noah Okafor scoring twice and Dominic Calvert-Lewin also on target. Daniel Farke reported no injuries before the Chelsea game, with Okafor, Anton Stach, Calvert-Lewin and Joe Rodon all back. Promoted Coventry sit 14th, three points above the drop zone, after a 3-2 home win over Crystal Palace, but Frank Lampard has doubts: Taiwo Awoniyi went off with an ankle problem against Palace and Caleb Yirenkyi has an ankle injury, and Luke Woolfenden, Aurele Amenda, Josh Eccles and Haji Wright are listed as out. The numbers have no missing players for either side and already count both teams' recent form (Leeds shooting more, Coventry scoring more than expected but winning few corners). No referee is named yet. Team news was still early when this was written, four days out, and no full preview for this match had been published, so the view is small.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals: 1.8 for Leeds and 1.0 for Coventry. Leeds' attack is flying after scoring four at Chelsea, and Coventry have conceded plenty lately, but the numbers already count that recent form. Their scorer Awoniyi limped off against Palace with an ankle injury and is a doubt, and the numbers don't know that, so I take a little off, to about 2.7.

corners.text: The numbers expect 8.3 corners: 5.2 for Leeds and 3.2 for Coventry. They already lower both sides for recent form, especially Coventry, whose games against them have produced few corners. Leeds attack with crosses and quick wide play, which fits that split. Nothing in the team news changes it, so I stay at about 8.3.

cards.text: The numbers expect 2.8 cards, with Coventry slightly more likely to be booked as the away side. They already count Leeds picking up more cards than usual lately and Coventry fewer. It is not a derby, no referee has been named yet, and neither side has a known ban, so I stay at about 2.8.

shots.text: The numbers expect 28.1 shots, with 18.5 of them from Leeds at home. That already includes Leeds shooting more than usual over their last six games. Okafor and Calvert-Lewin are both fit, which matches the numbers' picture of Leeds pushing at home. An Awoniyi absence would cost Coventry a little, but he is only a doubt, so I stay at about 28.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers expect 8.4 shots on target: 5.2 for Leeds and 3.2 for Coventry. Leeds' sharper recent finishing is already counted. Coventry's front line may be weakened if Awoniyi misses out, but that is not confirmed four days out, so I stay at about 8.4.
